questions.q: What is the author's central argument?
options: Slashing federal spending is the only realistic path to cutting the debt
Repeated tax cuts and high debt will limit what Democrats can afford to do
Democrats should raise taxes sharply to repay World War II era borrowing
A debt-to-GDP ratio of 100% is too low to worry anyone at home or abroad
questions.explain: The passage says debt has grown through repeated tax cuts and that Democrats will face hard choices because new borrowing now costs much more.

questions.q: How much did the series of tax cuts since 2001 add to the debt, per the Center for American Progress analysis?
questions.explain: The passage says the tax cuts since 2001 added over $10 trillion to the debt.

questions.q: Which tax cuts were the most expensive in history as a share of GDP?
questions.explain: Reagan's 1981 tax cuts were the most expensive, reducing annual revenue by an average 2.9% of GDP.

questions.q: What did the CBO project for debt by the end of 2034 under the 2025 bill?
questions.explain: The CBO projected increasing deficits would push debt to 116% of GDP by the end of 2034.

questions.q: Why did Trump's cuts, though small as a share of GDP, affect the debt so much?
options: They were paired with large new stimulus spending
Congress let most of the provisions expire after 2025
Borrowing costs were higher than in earlier eras
They cut revenue by more than Reagan's 1981 cuts did
questions.explain: The passage says the cuts had a larger debt effect partly because of the higher cost of borrowing.
